chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Shazan ibn al-Khalil who said, 'And I wrote from his book with a chain for him raising it to Isa ibn Abdullah,' he said, 'Isa ibn Abdullah said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'

'May I be sacrificed for you, what is worship?' He said: 'The good intention in obedience, from the aspects from which Allah is obeyed. Indeed, O Isa, you will not be a believer until you know the abrogating from the abrogated.'

He said, 'I said, may I be sacrificed for you, and what is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated?' So he said: 'Is it not that you are with the Imam, settling your self upon the good intention in his obedience, so that Imam passes away and another Imam comes, so you settle your self upon the good intention in his obedience?' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'This is the knowledge of the abrogating from the abrogated.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of worship and the meaning of knowing the abrogating and abrogated verses according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates 'good intention' (husn al-niyyah) as the essence of worship, linking it directly to the epistemological necessity of distinguishing between abrogating (naskh) and abrogated (mansukh) divine rulings. He contextualizes this knowledge within the framework of Imamate, illustrating that just as one Imam succeeds another with potentially new legal directives, the believer’s steadfast intention in obedience remains the constant anchor of faith. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that understanding the dynamic nature of revelation through the Imam is integral to true monotheistic practice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Shazaan Bin Al Khaleel who said, ‘And a letter from a letter of his, raising it to Isa Bin Abdullah said, ‘Isa Bin Abdullah said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘

May I be sacrificed for your<sup>asws</sup>! What is the worship?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The good intention in obedience (to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>) from the aspect which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> can be obeyed from. As for you, O Isa, you cannot become a Believer until you recognise the Abrogating from the Abrogated (Verses of the Holy Quran)’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>! And what is the recognition of the Abrgating from the Abrogated?’ So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Do you not happen to be with the Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, placed in your self upon the good intention, being in his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> obedience. So that Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> passes away and another Imam<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> comes, so you place yourself upon the good intention of being in his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> obedience?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘This is the recognition of the Abgrogating and the Abrogated’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Shadhan ibn al-Khalil. The narrator has said that he wrote down from his book through the chain of his narrators who narrated in a marfu’ manner from ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah saying: ‘“Isa ibn ‘Abd Allah once said to abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is worship?’ The Imam said, ‘It is good intention in obedience to Allah concerning the aspects through which He is obeyed. As for you, O ‘Isa, you will not be a believer until you can distinguish the abrogating from the abrogated.’

I then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is distinguishing the abrogating from the abrogated?’ The Imam said, ‘Is it not true that you obey an Imam with good intention and in good faith, and when that Imam passes away and another Imam comes, you settle your soul on obedience to him with good intention and in good faith?’ I said, ‘Yes, I do so.’ The Imam said, ‘This is distinguishing the abrogating from the abrogated.’”
